items.title: Eddie Johnson Interview, 1962-11-06
items.q: Who would he have in his man? George McCullough, of course, and myself. >> [INTERVIEWEE] Raymond Brown.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. I know he'd come down here sometime. Yeah. I don't want to see his name in advertisements, you know. Yeah. In the old newspapers all I can know. Old time people, yeah. I forget, did he play on the boat or not? No, no. Not on the boat, he was in the dances and stuff. No, he was playing on the boat. He used to play violin and led the band. So he did. Who would he have in his man? George McCullough, of course, and myself.
Raymond Brown. What did he play? Which one? Trombone. Trombone. He's dead now. Yeah.

There's two Raymond Browns, isn't it? His son's name was Raymond too, I think. Yeah. Trombone. Yeah, they called him Clifford or something, didn't they? Clifford Brown. I think his real name was Raymond, somebody told me. I can't remember who told me. I think Andy Anderson. Yeah, he's out of time, isn't he? Clifford? Clifford Brown. I think his real name was Raymond, somebody told me. They just called him Clifford to make the difference for father and son. I can't remember who told me. I think Andy Anderson.…
